evidence_summary: Guo et al. 2018 (PMID 30181118): human MSC knockdown inhibits osteogenic differentiation in vitro; mouse conditional knockout (MSC/pre-osteoblast-Cre, active during skeletal development/differentiation -- not adult-onset) causes low bone mass and impaired BMP2-driven regeneration via Smad1/RUNX2 destabilization.
species: Human (MSC, in vitro) + Mouse (conditional KO, postnatal-developmental)
reversible_or_developmental: developmental/postnatal conditional-KO phenotype; reversibility not tested
relevance_to_partial_inhibition: the human MSC arm used siRNA/shRNA knockdown (partial knockdown, not complete germline KO) and still showed impaired differentiation -- some relevance to partial pharmacological inhibition, though not a drug study

evidence_summary: Wigoda et al. 2026 (PMID 42315110): 6 individuals with heterozygous de novo USP34 LoF variants (5 confirmed de novo) -- neurodevelopmental syndrome including distal limb anomalies and craniofacial dysmorphism, overlapping 2p15p16.1 microdeletion syndrome.
reversible_or_developmental: developmental, congenital (present from birth) -- not an adult-onset or drug-induced phenotype
relevance_to_partial_inhibition: heterozygous LoF is itself a form of partial (50%) gene-dosage reduction, so this IS relevant context for a partial-inhibition drug, though the phenotype is congenital/developmental, not something a drug given to an adult would necessarily reproduce

No relevant skeletal-muscle-function evidence identified.

evidence_summary: NEW this pass, not in the prior phase: Vezf1 regulates cardiac structure and contractile function (PMID 31911272, EBioMedicine). VEZF1 expression is DECREASED in diseased human myocardium and mouse hearts (correlative, human+mouse disease-association). Zebrafish Vezf1 knockdown REDUCES cardiac growth and impairs ventricular contractile response to beta-adrenergic stimuli (does not affect Ca2+ transient kinetics). VEZF1 regulates cardiac-muscle-contraction and dilated-cardiomyopathy-related genes; Myh7/beta-MHC identified as a direct target via an MCAT promoter element; TEAD-1 identified as a VEZF1 binding partner at this element.
species: Human (myocardium expression, correlative) + Mouse (heart expression, correlative) + Zebrafish (knockdown, causal) + primary cardiomyocytes (mechanistic)
reversible_or_developmental: postnatal/adult zebrafish knockdown -- not an embryonic/developmental-only model; reversibility not tested
relevance_to_partial_inhibition: HIGH relevance -- knockdown (partial loss-of-function), not complete knockout, directly reduced cardiac growth/contractile function in an already-formed postnatal heart; this is the most drug-relevant liability finding identified for either gene in this phase
sources: PMID 31911272 (new this pass, full abstract fetched and verified)

evidence_summary: Homozygous Vezf1-null mice: embryonic lethal at midgestation (angiogenic remodeling defects, hemorrhaging, defective endothelial adhesion/tight junctions), PMID 15882861 (carried forward). Heterozygous: ~20%-penetrant lymphatic hypervascularization with hemorrhaging/edema.
reversible_or_developmental: developmental, embryonic-lethal (homozygous) -- must not be extrapolated to adult drug toxicity
zygosity: homozygous (lethal) and heterozygous (partial, incompletely penetrant) phenotypes both reported
relevance_to_partial_inhibition: the heterozygous (partial-dosage) phenotype is informative for partial-inhibition risk in principle, but is incompletely penetrant (~20%) and embryonic/developmental in origin, not adult

evidence_summary: A single 4-generation family with autosomal-dominant dilated cardiomyopathy carrying a heterozygous nonsense VEZF1 variant (p.Lys164*), segregating with disease in 8 affected members; functional assay showed failure to transactivate MYH7/EDN1 (carried forward). HOWEVER ClinGen's Dilated Cardiomyopathy Gene Curation Expert Panel formally classifies this gene-disease relationship as 'No Known Disease Relationship' (2026-03-04), disputing it. Both are reported; neither silently resolved.
relevance_to_partial_inhibition: disputed evidence -- see ClinGen caveat; if real, would be directly relevant (partial dosage loss -> cardiac phenotype)
